pr_title: Fix case where `h_separation` might not work in `Button`
pr_body:
<!--
Please target the `master` branch in priority.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.
You can mention in the description if the change is compatible with `3.x`.
-->

Fix #64140.
*Bugsquad edit:* Fixes #64371

| Before | After |
| :-------: | :-----: |
|![1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/183910901-a320985d-b077-40c0-8b06-0bd1b96100fd.gif)|![2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/183910941-8aa1eb48-bec8-4ef4-b34e-ae67183f6fe1.gif) |

~~Split from #59340.~~

There are still issues with the drawing and will be fixed in another PR.

Edit:
This patch mainly solves two things:
1. The typo of `h_separation`;
2. Negative values of `h_separation` will be treated as `0` when used, to prevent the button's minimum `width` from being reduced by `h_separation`.
pr_comments: You added me as co-author (GitHub does this automatically when you accept a suggestion).
Sorry, `h_separation` should be ignored when `expand_icon` is enabled.
Uh why should it be ignored? It's just a space between icon and text. If you expand icon and resize to 0, it's still there and separation should take effect. The previous behavior was alright.

For Button-derived classes with internal elements, `CheckBox`, `CheckButton`, `OptionButton`, may appear to be twice as long (the icon is hidden).

Of course, they behave inconsistently, and it's not clear to me which one to use as a standard.

Ah seems like CheckBox etc. apply the separation twice for their own icon.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/184125261-2345687a-40b3-4a9c-bbb2-aff9910bce57.png)
In this case ignoring separation makes sense.

But there is still no reason to ignore it in Button. You could either add a virtual method that tells whether this should be ignored or, more simple but not much used in the codebase, some `protected bool` property.

| version | picture |
| :-------: | :-------: |
|   v4.0.alpha13.official [82811367c] | ![alpha13](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/184286050-7dced3be-956d-4a6f-9958-de33f035a29f.png)|
| v4.0.alpha.custom_build [317ced820] | ![0](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/184286806-fab6e4b2-d7fd-4129-b5ae-fd8e2c33a16e.png) |
| v4.0.alpha.custom_build [323d611a6] | ![1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/184286062-159d0e80-3fb9-4699-b864-1f20e775b457.png) |

The table above is a comparison of the minimum size between versions. In the picture, the right node is a copy of the left node with `expand_icon` enabled.

I hope I have understood correctly what the expectation is like. `h_separation = 100`, please ignore those textures that are drawn incorrectly. 

There seem to be two kinds of `h_separation` currently:
1. The one between internal elements and custom elements (icon and text as a whole);
2. The one between custom elements (icon and text are treated independently).

The previous implementation seems to not want separation between icons, but if there is no separation at all, it feels crowded together.

I seem to be getting more and more deviated from the original intention. Now I only fix typo and restrict `h_separation` from being negative. 

When `h_separation` is non-negative, it should look the same as in alpha13

OptionButton minimum size seems broken:
![godot windows tools 64_3hNJ8pA3rH](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/184511937-d5ba285d-ddd2-43f4-8ef8-45a13bc4dba4.gif)

CheckBox center alignment makes the text go into separation area:
![godot windows tools 64_FkKmFR9U8f](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/184511953-be4b041d-d99e-4529-8e3a-eb7182e71de6.gif)
The worst part is that it's more to the left than Left alignment. CheckButton has similar problem.

> I assume [#64218 (comment)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/64218#issuecomment-1211818278) is addressed in #64351?

I guess no, both patches are trying to get back to alpha13. Except that a negative `h_separation` is treated as `0`, and limits the extent to which the `text`/`icon` can be drawn. These changes between alpha13 should be intuitively found from comparing `png`s in #64351.

This issue in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/64218#issuecomment-1211818278 also exists in alpha13. 

I'm a little unclear on what exactly it should look like. So had to use alpha13 as a reference. If there is something wrong in alpha13, I will fix it later. I'm a little concerned about over-modification causing other regressions.

It might be better to figure out what it should look like first.


1. internal element (`i_icon`)
  1.1 existence
2. custom elements
  2.1. custom icon (`icon`)
    2.1.1. existence
    2.1.2. `expand_icon`
    2.1.3. `icon_alignment`
  2.2. custom text (`text`)
    2.2.1. existence 
    2.2.2. `clip_text`
    2.2.3. text `alignment`
  2.3. separation between custom elements (`s1`)
3. separation between internal element and custom elements (`s0`)

The above will directly and indirectly affect the minimum size.
In alpha13, if there are only `icon` and `i_icon`, `s0` is ignored. It's a little different when if `i_icon`, `icon`, `text` all exists.

![captrue](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/184520153-21d98043-dd46-49d8-9c9d-00d253e9abc3.png)
The documentation's description and the actual drawing in alpha13 are inconsistent.

![1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/184520255-8779b041-b4eb-46a1-a5a1-ef4cb41a7512.png)
The actual drawing in alpha13 and your suggestions are inconsistent.

I haven't looked into the button's design criteria, so I'm a little confused.

However, this patch is intended to fix typo to get it back to a slightly better state.

issue_context.title: Inspector buttons are missing padding on the right side
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.alpha14.official [106b68050]

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Inspector buttons are missing padding on the right side of the text.

| Alpha 13 | Alpha 14 |
---|---
| ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67974470/184504374-8cef0821-cdd4-4d17-a619-8ff10f2b2905.png) | ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67974470/184504282-ce62bc3f-7fc0-40e3-b7a8-6e898463f622.png) |

### Steps to reproduce

* Select a node.
* Look at the Add Metadata button at the bottom of the inspector.

review_comments: This change makes it impossible to have negative `h_separation`. I don't think it's necessary to limit it (or at least the limitation should be documented).

A negative value of `h_separation` is meaningless, otherwise, it may make `minsize.width` smaller, become `0` or even a **negative** value (even if there is an icon or text). In some cases this can result in insufficient visible space for drawing.

It makes the text overlap icon. Weird, but maybe someone wants it.
Limit it is fine too, I guess. But as I said, it should be documented in the property description.
